placements.why: The graph and strata for this repo are both empty, and this envelope's entire content — a spectrograph's calibration value and its verification against reference plates — is calibration-grain material with no existing strata category to hold it. Nothing supplied is close enough to call this an extension of anything else, so it stands as a foundational, standalone strata mint rather than a subordinate of any existing node.
placements.title: Calibration as its own organizational category
placements.theme: Claims of instrument readiness are organized under a distinct calibration category, separate from strategy, product, or architecture work.

placements.title: Calibration claims are trusted only once checked against a dated reference standard
placements.theme: An instrument's calibration value is not asserted on its own — it is confirmed by re-checking it against a fixed prior reference across the full operating range.
placements.why: src-1/src-3 assert the calibration value (88.4 MHz) in prose and structured form, and src-2/src-4 assert the verification method (checked against June reference plates, holding across the full band) in the same two renderings — the position pass already reads all four as one calibration event. The specific 88.4 MHz reading and the specific June plates are position-grain facts (per the grain test, a one-time measurement is evidence, not a leaf), but the underlying subject — that a calibration is only credible once checked against a dated reference standard across the operating band — is a theme future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other dates, other reference sets) would keep feeding. No existing leaf or hub was supplied to hold this, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata, which is its natural, exact home rather than any looser fit.
